t.1.18.1: Sūta said: All this has been told to you, how the amṛta was churned, at which the glorious horse of matchless prowess arose.
t.1.18.2: Seeing him then, Kadrū said this to Vinatā: "Of what color is Uccaiḥśravas, good lady? Find out without delay."
t.1.18.3: This king of horses is surely white; or what do you think, fair one? You too tell me his colour; then on this point there will be cause for a wager.
t.1.18.5: Having thus made a mutual agreement, with servitude as the stake, the two went to their own homes, saying, "Tomorrow we shall see."
t.1.18.4: Kadrū said: I believe this horse has a black tail, O bright-smiling one. Come and wager with me, with servitude as the stake, O beautiful lady.
t.1.18.6: Then Kadrū, wishing to work deceit, commanded her thousand sons: "Become hairs as dark as collyrium!"
t.1.18.7: "Enter the horse quickly, so that I may not become a slave!" When they did not comply with that command, she cursed those serpents.
t.1.18.8: When the snake sacrifice of the wise royal seer Janamejaya, descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, is under way, the fire will burn you up.
t.1.18.10: Together with all the hosts of gods, he approved that speech, seeing the great multitude of the serpents and desiring the welfare of all creatures.
t.1.18.9: The Grandfather himself heard this exceedingly cruel curse that Kadrū had pronounced, for it was truly uttered through the working of fate.
t.1.18.11: For these biting serpents are mighty and possess venom of fierce potency. Because of their sharp venom, and for the welfare of all creatures, he gave the great-souled Kāśyapa the knowledge that destroys poison.
